what-is-personal-finance.title: What is Personal Finance
what-is-personal-finance.content: Personal finance is how you manage your money: earning, spending, saving, and investing. In the Philippines, this often includes supporting family (breadwinner), managing remittances (OFW), and planning for goals like education, housing, and retirement. Good habits help you build an emergency fund, pay off debt, and reach goals without stress.

budgeting.title: Budgeting
budgeting.content: A simple rule is 50/30/20: 50% to needs (rent, utilities, food, transport), 30% to wants, 20% to savings and debt paydown. Track spending for a month first, then set limits per category. Automate savings so you save before spending. In the Philippines, breadwinners may need to allocate more to needs; aim to keep at least 10–20% for savings.

debt.title: Debt
debt.content: Not all debt is bad—education or an affordable home can be worthwhile. High-interest consumer debt (credit cards, unsecured loans) is costly. Keep monthly debt payments below 36% of net income. Paying more than the minimum on high-interest debt saves interest and shortens the term. Two common strategies: Avalanche (highest interest first) and Snowball (smallest balance first).

emergency-fund.title: Emergency Fund
emergency-fund.content: Aim for 3–6 months of essential expenses in a separate, accessible account. If you're a breadwinner or OFW with dependents, aim for 6–12 months. Use average monthly expenses (rent, utilities, food, minimum debt payments) as the basis. Keep it in a high-yield savings or time deposit—not in long-term investments—so you can access it quickly in a job loss or medical emergency.

investing-basics.title: Investing Basics
investing-basics.content: Build an emergency fund and pay down high-interest debt first. Then consider Pag-IBIG MP2, SSS, UITFs, or index funds. Conservative options (time deposits, bonds) offer lower return and lower risk; equity can grow more over the long term but with more volatility. Match your choices to your goal horizon and risk tolerance.

insurance.title: Insurance
insurance.content: Insurance protects your family and assets from large, unexpected costs (death, illness, accident). For breadwinners and OFWs, life and health coverage can ensure dependents are not left in difficulty. Start with life and health insurance that fits your budget. Compare term life vs whole life; often term is cheaper for the same coverage. Consider PhilHealth and employer plans, then top up with private insurance if needed.

goal-planning.title: Goal Planning
goal-planning.content: Set goals that are specific, measurable, and time-bound. For example: 'Save ₱500,000 for emergency fund in 24 months.' Prices rise over time (often 3–5% per year in the PH), so when planning for a future amount use inflation-adjusted targets: target today × (1 + inflation rate)^years. PesoSense computes this for you and shows how much to save each month under different return scenarios.
